_note: Global sim numbers lifted from the prototype. Seconds unless a key says otherwise; distances in logical px.

world._note: Per-world settings (design 14 §9.1 day length, 00 §2 Gentle, 00 §4 Safe, 14 §6 Pets safe, 14 §1 rule 7). dayChoices: the day lengths a world may have, seconds at 1x (night is the last nightFrac of every day). first: a player's first world; later: every world made after it. sim: what the sim uses when a caller gives no settings, i.e. the tools: the prototype's 60 s day, Safe on, no Gentle, no Pets safe, so recorded worlds and the statistical gate stay comparable (14 §9.1).

path._note: Bible 01 §7. Ticks where a key says so; distances in logical px; sepPush in px per second (0.5 px a tick), given on one step in sepEvery (design 14 §7 T2), never to a creature alone in its cell.

save._note: Autosave (design 14 §7 T1, 03 §10): every everyTicks steps (600 = 30 s at 1x), or everySec of real time after a change that is not saved yet (painting while paused, a slow phone), and when the page is hidden.

undo._note: Undo (design 14 §3): how many of the player's steps can be taken back.

hand._note: The Hand tool (design 14 §3): a creature lifted by the player is out of the world (inside = HELD) until dropped. dropAlt: the height a dropped humanoid comes down from, by parachute (the UFO's chuteAlt); hopAlt: the little fall of anything else.

harm._note: Design 14 §6, the harm matrix: what each source of harm may do to a creature, by what protects it. safe: a creature Safe guards (a human while Safe is on; a pet, and later a renamed creature, while Pets safe is on). gentle: a creature Gentle covers (00 §2). neither: no protection. Effects, most protective first: block (the source stops; an attacker shows ? and wanders; a creature that would hunt a guarded one within balkRadius px balks the same way on its think tick), none (no damage; the rest of the event still happens), floor (never below 1 hp), floorFirst (floor in the player's first world, else normal), warn (damage only after warnSec in the hazard, a warning shown meanwhile), normal. null: the column has no say. When both protections apply, the more protective effect wins. The code reads this table (src/sim/harm.js); its fixtures are tools/fixtures.mjs harm-*.

react._note: Reactions (design 14 §5). cooldownSec: how long a (row, A, B) pair waits before that row can fire for them again, unless the row says otherwise. maxDepth: how deep one reaction may set off another. tileCap: tile effects in one step, world-wide; the overflow is dropped in file order. placedTiles: how near a new thing must be to another for the placed trigger. coolMax: how many cooldowns are remembered before the spent ones are swept. followSec, tameSec: how long a following or a tamed creature stays that way when a row does not say.

fire._note: Basic fire (design 14 §7 T9): burn, spread, extinguish, regrow. burnSec: how long one tile burns. spread: the chance per second that a burning tile lights one neighbour (rolled on the sim's own stream, so two worlds burn alike). rainOut: how many times faster fire burns down in rain. regrowSec: how long burnt ground takes to come back. dps: damage a second to whoever stands in it (through the harm table as a reaction, 14 §6).
